messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: How can I summarize methylation information over CpG islands instead of fixed base-pair windows using tileMethylCounts
parts:
Hi Sumithra,
you can use regionCounts() function for that, check the function help and also an example is below: 

data(methylKit)
example.file=system.file("extdata", "cpgi.hg18.bed.txt", package = "methylKit")

cpg.obj=read.feature.flank(example.file,feature.flank.name=c("CpGi","shores")) # read CpGi  and shores

CpGi.methylRawList=regionCounts(methylObj=methylRawList.obj, regions=cpg.obj$CpGi)


The CpG island file should be in BED format and will be read in as GRanges object. If you can get GRanges object for CpG islands by other means you can also use that in regionCounts() function. If you want to learn how to download annotation files (the ones available in UCSC) in BED format see:
https://code.google.com/p/methylkit/#Downloading_Annotation_Files

Best,
Altuna

parts:
I tried the following to get methylation stats for CpG islands in the K562 methylation datasets from ENCODE. It worked except for the warning after the cpg.obj step:

library(methylKit)
file.list = list("wgEncodeHaibMethylRrbsK562HaibSitesRep1.bed.gz",
                 "wgEncodeHaibMethylRrbsK562HaibSitesRep2.bed.gz")
obj = read(file.list, sample.id = list("test", "control"), treatment = c(1,0),
           assembly = "hg19", header = FALSE, context = "CpG", resolution = "base",
           pipeline = list(fraction = FALSE, chr.col = 1, start.col = 3, end.col = 3,
                          coverage.col = 5, strand.col = 6, freqC.col = 11))

data(methylKit)
example.file=system.file("extdata", "cpgi.hg18.bed.txt", package = "methylKit")

cpg.obj=read.feature.flank(example.file,feature.flank.name=c("CpGi","shores")) # read CpGi  and shores

Warning message:
In .Seqinfo.mergexy(x, y) :
  Each of the 2 combined objects has sequence levels not in the other:
  - in 'x': chr21_random, chr22_random
  - in 'y': chr1, chr10, chr11, chr12, chr13, chr14, chr15, chr16, chr17, chr18, chr19, chr2, chr3, chr4, chr5, chr6, chr7, chr8, chr9, chrM, chrX, chrY
  Make sure to always combine/compare objects based on the same reference
  genome (use suppressWarnings() to suppress this warning).


CpGi.methylRawList=regionCounts(methylObj=obj[[1]], regions=cpg.obj$CpGi)

getMethylationStats(CpGi.methylRawList,plot=T) #gave a histogram of % methylation per region

Did the code work despite the warning?
Thanks--Sumithra
